answer: Charge a creation fee that grows quadratically with how many identities one funder has already spawned: the first costs a little, the tenth costs a hundred times more, so a sybil farmer hits a summit of expense long before his clones matter. Honest newcomers pay almost nothing, and the fee funds a shared haven — a public insurance pool that compensates victims of fraud. Funding-source clustering links the clones, so splitting wallets cannot reset the price; only a genuine grove of unrelated sponsors keeps costs low. Limit: clustering can mislabel honest groups sharing one treasury.
